name: Distilled water
summary: Water purified by distillation so that dissolved salts and impurities are removed.
handling: No special hazards. Keep the container closed so it stays pure.

name: Hydrochloric acid (dilute)
summary: A strong acid. In solution it releases hydrogen ions, giving a very low pH.
handling: The concentrated acid burns skin and gives off irritating fumes, so handle it in a fume hood with gloves and goggles.

name: Sodium hydroxide solution (dilute)
summary: A strong alkali, also called caustic soda. It releases hydroxide ions and gives a very high pH.
handling: Even dilute solutions damage the eyes. Wear goggles, and store it in plastic because it slowly attacks glass.

name: Acetic acid (vinegar strength)
summary: A weak acid. It is the acid that gives vinegar its sour taste and smell.
handling: Glacial (concentrated) acetic acid is flammable and corrosive. Vinegar-strength solutions are much milder.

name: Sodium hydrogen carbonate solution
summary: Baking soda dissolved in water. A mild alkali that releases carbon dioxide when it reacts with acids.
handling: Low hazard. Avoid contact with the eyes.

name: Universal indicator
summary: A blend of indicator dyes that shows a different colour across the whole pH range, from red (acidic) to purple (alkaline).
handling: Usually made up in ethanol, so keep it away from flames.

name: Phenolphthalein indicator
summary: An indicator that is colourless in acidic and neutral solutions and turns pink in alkaline ones.
handling: Usually made up in ethanol. Phenolphthalein itself is a suspected health hazard, so avoid skin contact.

name: Copper(II) sulfate solution
summary: A bright blue solution of copper ions, widely used in school and analytical chemistry.
handling: Harmful if swallowed and toxic to aquatic life. Collect waste rather than pouring it down the sink.

name: Iron(III) chloride solution
summary: A yellow-orange solution of iron(III) ions.
handling: Corrosive to skin, eyes and metals. Wear gloves and goggles.

name: Potassium thiocyanate solution
summary: A colourless solution used as a sensitive test for iron(III) ions.
handling: Harmful if swallowed, inhaled or absorbed through skin. Never mix it with strong acids, which can release toxic gas.

name: Silver nitrate solution
summary: A colourless solution of silver ions, used to test for chloride, bromide and iodide ions.
handling: Stains skin black and is very toxic to aquatic life. Store it in a dark bottle, as light breaks it down.

name: Sodium chloride solution
summary: Common salt dissolved in water. A source of chloride ions.
handling: Low hazard.

name: Hydrogen peroxide (3%)
summary: A colourless liquid that slowly breaks down into water and oxygen. Catalysts make this happen very quickly.
handling: Concentrated solutions are strong oxidisers and burn skin. Store it cool and in the dark.

name: Potassium iodide solution
summary: A colourless solution of iodide ions. It catalyses the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide.
handling: Low hazard in dilute form. Avoid swallowing.

name: Starch solution
summary: A slightly cloudy solution of soluble starch, used as an indicator for iodine.
handling: Low hazard. Make it fresh, as it spoils within days.

name: Iodine solution
summary: Iodine dissolved in potassium iodide solution. It is brown and turns blue-black with starch.
handling: Stains skin and clothes. Iodine vapour irritates the eyes and lungs.

name: Liquid detergent
summary: Washing-up liquid. Its surfactants lower surface tension and trap gas as foam.
handling: Can irritate the eyes. Rinse with plenty of water.

name: Ethanol
summary: A clear, volatile alcohol and one of the most widely used laboratory solvents.
handling: Highly flammable liquid and vapour. Keep it away from flames and hot surfaces.

name: Acetone
summary: A fast-evaporating solvent that dissolves many plastics, oils and resins.
handling: Highly flammable. Its vapour can cause drowsiness, so use it in a ventilated area.

name: Sulfuric acid
summary: A dense, strong mineral acid that is also a powerful dehydrating agent.
handling: Causes severe burns. Always add acid to water, never water to acid.

name: Nitric acid
summary: A strong, oxidising mineral acid that dissolves most metals.
handling: Causes severe burns and gives off toxic fumes. Use it only in a fume hood, away from organic materials.

name: Potassium permanganate
summary: Dark purple crystals that make intensely purple solutions. It is a strong oxidising agent.
handling: Keep it away from combustible materials. It stains skin brown and is toxic to aquatic life.

name: Ammonia solution
summary: Ammonia gas dissolved in water. A weak alkali with a sharp smell.
handling: The vapour irritates the eyes and lungs. Open bottles in a fume hood.

name: Methanol
summary: The simplest alcohol, used as a solvent and as a raw material for other chemicals.
handling: Toxic if swallowed, inhaled or absorbed through skin, and can cause blindness. Highly flammable.

name: D-Glucose
summary: A simple sugar and the main energy source for living cells.
handling: Low hazard. Keep it dry and sealed.

name: Calcium carbonate
summary: A white powder found in chalk, limestone and marble.
handling: Low hazard. Avoid breathing in the dust.

name: Agar powder
summary: A gelling agent made from seaweed, used to set culture media in petri dishes.
handling: Low hazard. Avoid breathing in the dust.

name: Glycerol
summary: A thick, colourless, sweet-tasting liquid that mixes with water.
handling: Low hazard. It is very slippery when spilled.
